cv.name: Ayesha Khan
cv.headline: Backend developer: Go, PostgreSQL and double-entry ledgers
cv.summary: Backend developer who built and runs a double-entry bookkeeping API in Go and PostgreSQL for a two-branch store, and cut month-end closing from 3 days to 2 hours by automating reconciliation. Currently learning Kubernetes and AWS.

bullets: Cut month-end closing from 3 days to 2 hours by automating reconciliation.
Built the store's bookkeeping API in Go and PostgreSQL, replacing a paper ledger across two branches.
The API posts about 400 ledger entries a day with sub-50ms queries on a $5 VPS.
Deployed with Docker on a single VPS, with nightly backups to Google Cloud Storage.
Wrote integration tests that caught 12 regressions before release.
Contributed to a REST API for a logistics client in Node.js and TypeScript.

projects.name: LedgerLite
projects.description: A double-entry bookkeeping API for small shops, written in Go with PostgreSQL and sqlc.
highlights: Runs 3 years of transactions for 2 shops.

projects.name: tokio-tracing-fix
projects.description: An upstream fix for a span leak in Rust tracing-subscriber when spans were dropped across await points.
highlights: Span memory in a worker dropped from 1.2 GB to 140 MB over a day of traffic.

projects.name: Pixel Pantry
projects.description: A recipe-sharing PWA that works offline.
highlights: 300 home cooks used it during the beta.

emphasis: Opened with ledger correctness and the month-end result
Go and PostgreSQL first in skills, in the posting’s words
